tip: Proper names take an apostrophe before case endings: Ankara'da means in Ankara, the -da part meaning in or at.
To ask someone for something, put -dan on the person: Komşudan ... istedim is literally requested from the neighbor.
hiçbir şey (nothing) still needs a negative verb: hiçbir şey istemedim, both halves negative, means wanted nothing.
Adding -la to a noun makes a manner adverb: şaşkınlıkla means with surprise, from şaşkınlık plus -la.
yardım etmek (to help) takes the dative, since help goes to someone: hence birbirlerine, to each other, carries -e.
beri (since) follows a noun in the ablative: Sabahtan beri means since morning, sabah plus -tan plus beri.
Possession marks both words: in Annemin yemekleri the owner takes -in and the thing owned takes -leri.
After a length of time, önce means ago: Üç yıl önce is three years ago.
The -miş past reports something not personally witnessed: gelmiş means it has come, so the story goes, unlike plain geldi.
Comparison uses -dan plus daha: yaz aylarından çok daha soğuk means much colder than summer months.
The aorist -ir/-ar marks habits: gelir and yapar mean she regularly comes and cooks, not a one-time event.
Clock times take the locative -de/-te: saat üçte means at three o'clock.
sonra (after) follows a noun in the ablative: Yemekten sonra means after the meal, yemek plus -ten.
